question: Which moderate leader, often referred to as the 'Grand Old Man of India,' became the first Indian elected to the British House of Commons and helped shape the early nationalist movement?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Dadabhai Naoroji**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji** was a prominent moderate leader and is often referred to as the '**Grand Old Man of India**'.
 
• He was the first Indian to be elected to the **British House of Commons** in 1892 as a member of the Liberal Party.
 
• He played a critical role in shaping the **early nationalist movement** in India.
 
• Dadabhai Naoroji authored the famous book "**Poverty and Un-British Rule in India**", where he highlighted the economic drain caused by British rule.
 
• He was one of the founding members of the **Indian National Congress** in 1885, which later became the leading organization in India's independence movement.
 
• Naoroji was instrumental in articulating the idea of **Swaraj (self-rule)**, laying the groundwork for future freedom struggles.
 
• He advocated for Indian representation and rights in British administration and worked tirelessly to raise awareness about India's plight in Britain.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rash Behari Ghosh**__

 __
 
• **Rash Behari Ghosh** was an Indian lawyer, politician, and philanthropist.
 
• He served as the **President of the Indian National Congress** in 1907 and 1908.
 
• He was known for his moderate political stance and contributions to social reforms.
 
 
 
• **Gopal Krishna Gokhale**__
 __
 
• **Gopal Krishna Gokhale** was another prominent moderate leader and the founder of the **Servants of India Society**.
 
• He was a mentor to **Mahatma Gandhi** and emphasized constitutional reforms and non-violent methods.
 
• He played a significant role in advocating for Indian self-rule through gradual reforms.
 
 
 
• **Pherozeshah Mehta**__
 
 
• **Pherozeshah Mehta** was a distinguished lawyer and politician from Bombay.
 
• He was one of the founding members of the **Indian National Congress** and served as its President in 1890.
 
• He was nicknamed the "**Lion of Bombay**" for his leadership and contributions to Indian politics.
